newsitem.title: CHINA: Cable & Wireless in China telecom pact.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless in China telecom pact.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc said on Friday it had reached a preliminary agreement with Chinese telecommunications authorities on future cooperation, including plans for a fibre-optic submarine cable linking China and North America.
The memorandum of understanding was a broad framework for future cooperation with China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, Cable & Wireless chief executive Richard Brown told reporters.
Cable & Wireless officials said the first project under this cooperation accord would be to develop proposals for the submarine cable.
They did not say when work might begin, how much the project might cost or how financing might be structured.
Officials said, however, that a similar fibre-optic cable project spanning the Atlantic Ocean was expected to cost between $400 million and $500 million.

An existing joint venture company set up with the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications and the Shanghai Posts and Telecommunications Authority would play a role in the installation and maintenance of the cable.
Cable & Wireless has 49 percent of that venture and the Chinese side has a combined 51 percent.
Cable & Wireless also has its own fleet of cable ships. Company officials said the firm also had 1/12 of the world's undersea fibre-optic capacity.

The cooperation pact also calls for Cable & Wireless to play a role in providing telecommunications service aimed at multinational companies operating in China, officials said. They gave no further details.
They added that the accord also calls for an expansion of existing training programmes for Chinese telecommunications employees with the latest accord covering training for senior management.
Cable & Wireless announced the accord shortly after it formally opened a representative office in Beijing.
